title: Regional throughput floor + sticky-routing evacuation protocol
creator: Arielle Gomez
description: Implement a coordinated mechanism that guarantees a configurable regional "throughput floor" for reserved dedicated customers while enabling sticky-routing and a graceful evacuation protocol during zone-level incidents or maintenance. This ticket covers placement controller changes, allocation token mechanics, failover choreography, and runbook updates so that reserved capacity customers experience minimal disruption and we preserve data-residency constraints.
background: Customers on Dedicated pools have been requesting clearer guarantees when zones are drained for maintenance or experiencing transient failures. Today we either spill traffic immediately (causing latency spikes / dropped tokens) or perform naive cross-zone failover that can violate residency constraints. We need a middle path: keep a guaranteed minimum throughput in-region (throughput floor) by orchestrating soft-drain windows, sticky routing for long-lived connections, and controlled spillover to nearby regions only when policy allows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Placement controller exposes a per-customer 'regional_throughput_floor' setting (tokens/sec) and honors it during zone drains

2) During a simulated single-zone evacuation test, customers with a regional_throughput_floor set retain >= 80% of baseline throughput within the region for 10 minutes post-drain-initiation without violating data_residency=true constraints
3) Sticky-routing implemented so in-flight sessions with KV cache rehydrate to new allocations within the region without cache loss in >= 90% of cases
4) Evacuation protocol provides a configurable soft-drain window (default 120s) with progressive spillover steps and automatic rollback on capacity recovery
5) New dashboards and alerts created: Dedicated -> Throughput Floor Compliance, Evacuation Progress, Regional Spillover Rate; alert fires on <75% compliance for P0 customers
6) Runbook added to ops playbooks with step-by-step failover, manual override, and postmortem checklist
7) Backwards-compatible API/console surfaces: customers can set 'regional_throughput_floor' and 'residency_policy' via Console and API; settings validated in UI and gated by entitlement
design_notes: We will introduce a lightweight 'reservation token' that tags allocations with a customer and a locality score. Tokens are used by the scheduler to bias placement even under constrained capacity.

Sticky-routing will leverage existing session affinity machinery but add a 'soft-bind' layer: allocations can be migrated (with KV cache snapshot) during the soft-drain window rather than being killed immediately.

Evacuation choreography: 1) announce soft-drain + pre-warm within region, 2) enforce throughput floor using reservation tokens and scheduler bias, 3) progressive spillover to approved regions according to residency policy, 4) hard-drain if evacuation extends beyond configured TTL.
We will not modify billing semantics in this ticket; economics will be handled in follow-ups. The initial rollout should default floors to 0 to avoid accidental guarantees for all customers.

Policy models: residency_policy: [regional_only, allow_nearby_on_emergency, allow_anywhere]. For 'regional_only' we cannot spill traffic outside region; if capacity can't satisfy floor then customers will be routed to degraded-mode (queue with 503s annotated) and alerted.
Scheduler changes will add a locality_score computed from zone_preference, hot_cache_affinity, and reservation_token weight. This is additive to existing cost model and tunable via feature flag.

We will create a simulator to model different drain scenarios (traffic shapes, committed capacity mixes) to tune default soft-drain durations and floor percentages. See /docs/simulators/regional_floor_simulation.md
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API + Console - allow customers to configure regional_throughput_floor and residency_policy (backend validation + entitlement checks)
Phase 2: Scheduler + Tokens - introduce reservation_token and locality_score updates, feature-flagged scheduler bias, unit + e2e tests
Phase 3: Sticky Routing - implement soft-bind allocation migration and KV cache snapshot/restore primitives; integration tests with chat sessions
Phase 4: Evacuation Orchestrator - implement soft-drain windows, progressive spillover algorithm, and TTL-based hard-drain fallback
Phase 5: Observability + Runbook - dashboards, alerts, synthetic tests, and ops playbook placement
Phase 6: Canary - roll out to 5 reserved customers in us-west1 with staged monitoring for 72h
monitoring: Evacuation progress panel (percent of allocations migrated / remaining)
Alert: DedicatedThroughputFloorNoncompliance -> fires if P0 customers fall below configured floor for >5m
SLOs: latency P95 increase during evacuation must be < 30% for customers with floors; error rate increase < 1%
Synthetic tests: scheduled evacuations in staging triggered nightly to validate orchestration
runbook: Pre-checks: validate capacity headroom in region, confirm pre-warmed pools >= required warming tokens
Kickoff: set soft-drain at zone level via orchestrator UI (default 120s), monitor Evacuation progress dashboard
If compliance < target: increase pre-warm pool or extend soft-drain by 60s
If still failing and residency_policy allows: trigger progressive spillover to nearest region (follow list in residency table)
If residency_policy == regional_only and still failing: notify customer success & engineering; enable degraded-mode queue and open incident
Rollback: cancel soft-drain and mark allocations as non-evacuating to allow scheduler to reattach traffic
Post-incident: run postmortem checklist, collect KV cache migration logs, and produce customer-facing incident summary
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Scheduler bias could cause hot-spotting and underutilization. Mitigation: limit bias weight and enforce capacity packing heuristics; run simulator before ramp.

Risk: KV cache snapshot/restore adds latency and complexity. Mitigation: implement snapshot elision for cold sessions and validate incremental restore approach; add circuit breaker if restore latency > 500ms.
Risk: Misconfiguration allows accidental guarantees for small tenants. Mitigation: entitlement gating, UI warnings, and default floor=0 unless explicit opt-in.
Risk: Regulatory violation if spillover accidentally crosses data-sovereignty boundary. Mitigation: residency_policy enforced at allocation layer and additional unit tests covering edge cases.
Risk: Monitoring gaps. Mitigation: synthetic test coverage + alerting on missing telemetry for any evacuation operation
